attempted_claim: Let G be a simple adjoint algebraic group of type E_6, E_7, or E_8 over an algebraic closure of F_p, let F be a Frobenius endomorphism with p good for G, and let ell != p. For every semisimple ell'-element s in (G^*)^F whose connected centralizer C_{G^*}^o(s) is not a Levi subgroup (so the associated union B_s of ell-blocks is isolated), does the ell-decomposition matrix of B_s admit a lower-unitriangular basic set, ordered by the unipotent supports of the corresponding Jordan-decomposed characters? Equivalently, can one construct the required basic set and projective rows by Deligne-Lusztig/character-sheaf and (ell-)Kawanaka methods for all such isolated B_s?
decisive_failure: The lane establishes a methods-coverage obstruction, not a mathematical disproof of any single instance: no isolated decomposition matrix was computed and no counterexample to unitriangularity in a specific block was proved. The three gap instances reuse the published Bonnafe quasi-isolated classification and standard bad-prime data, and the literature boundary rests on hypothesis comparison against cited theorems rather than full-text re-derivation of each result.
